violations.scope: Sleeve 1d only. Phase 4 daily regime engine (v7.1) is PIT-clean.

gate0_pit.c9_vt_dd_same_day: CLEAN — DD lagged properly. VT applied within run_monthly_simulation (lookback window).

gate4_statistical.notes: FF5 alpha 11.86% (t=2.61, p=0.011). All 3 models significant at 5%.

gate5_diversification.notes: IDENTICAL performance to STR_1070 and STR_1085 (SR 1.333, CAGR 22.66%, MDD 24.81% — all digits match). STR_1070 claimed Risk Parity weighting and STR_1085 claimed Quality Gate, yet output is byte-identical. These 3 strategies are effective CLONES — only 1 should count as independent.

independence_analysis.evidence: Identical performance.csv (all 12 metrics match to 2dp), identical analysis_multifactor.csv (FF5 alpha to 15 decimal places), identical hurdle alpha_trend and OOS.
independence_analysis.root_cause_1070: STR_1070 claims HRP->RP weighting change, but in Phase 2 the function calc_gerber_mad_detoned_hrp_weights still uses .hrp_bisect (line 369 of STR_1060) vs 1/sigma (line 369-370 of STR_1070). The RP weights get overridden or the function produces identical results because HRP and naive RP converge with 5 low-correlation sleeves.
independence_analysis.root_cause_1085: STR_1085 applies Quality Gate (PiotroskiF<3 or IsZombie removal) BUT uses latest_qual = which.max(Factor_Date) across ALL history — this is SURVIVORSHIP BIAS (C6). Moreover, output is identical to STR_1060 meaning the gate removed zero tickers or the gate filtering had no effect on selected sleeves.
independence_analysis.conclusion: All 3 are parameter variants of the same STR_1036 base architecture. Count as 1 independent strategy.
